File No. 7974
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
S.1, Special Branch. XXXX,
SECRET REPORT
Date. February 3, 1937.
Subject Shanghai Operators Service and Frederic Leslie Shunaman.
Made by. and Forwarded by. D.S.I. Coyne

The Shanghai Operators Service and Frederic Leslie
Shunaman were the subjects of a letter dated August 8, 1936,
from the United States Consul General to the Commissioner of
Police in which information was requested concerning Shunaman
and his associates.
As a result of enquiries made by the Special Branch
a report was forwarded on August 26, 1936 in which particulars
regarding the opening of the Shanghai Operators Service by
Shunaman were given, but up to that time nothing had been dis-
covered regarding his associates.
No further enquiries were made regarding Shunaman until
January 1937 when information was received from a Chinese
Government agent to the effect that it was believed that the
Red Armies in Western China had foreign agents in Shanghai.
In searching for a person who might have taken over
the duty of Leon Minster, who was at one time engaged in
purchasing radio equipment for the Red Armies, the possibility
that Shunaman might be engaged in this work occurred to the under-
signed.
At the United States Consulate General it was learned
that Shunaman was born at Leominster, Mass. U.S.A. on March 13,
1901 and that his father became a naturalized citizen in 1908.
He is in possession of Passport No.198985. His wife Yetta
Shunaman (nee Gabin) was born in Bessarabia, South Russia, and
took out naturalization papers on December 4, 1917. She is in
possession of passport No.264114.
(Although it may be a coincident, worthy of note is the fact
that Shunaman was born at Leominster and is believed to have
relieved Leon Minster.)

档案编号 7974
上海公共租界工部局警务处。
S.1，特务科。XXXX，
秘密报告
日期：1937年2月3日。
主题：上海报务员服务社（Shanghai Operators Service）及弗雷德里克·莱斯利·舒纳曼（Frederic Leslie Shunaman）。
制作及呈送人：副督察长（D.S.I.）科因（Coyne）

美国总领事于1936年8月8日致函警务处处长，信中要求提供有关舒纳曼及其同伙的信息，上海报务员服务社及弗雷德里克·莱斯利·舒纳曼即为此信的主题。

经特务科查询后，于1936年8月26日呈送了一份报告，其中提供了舒纳曼开办上海报务员服务社的详细情况，但截至当时，尚未发现关于其同伙的任何信息。

在1937年1月之前，未再对舒纳曼进行进一步查询。此时收到一名中国政府特工的情报，称据信中国西部的红军在上海有外国代理人。

在搜寻可能接替莱昂·明斯特（Leon Minster）职责的人选时——明斯特曾从事为红军购买无线电设备的工作——卑职想到舒纳曼可能正从事此项工作。

从美国总领事馆获悉，舒纳曼于1901年3月13日出生于美国马萨诸塞州莱奥明斯特（Leominster），其父于1908年归化入籍。他持有护照第198985号。其妻耶塔·舒纳曼（Yetta Shunaman，婚前姓加宾/Gabin）出生于南俄比萨拉比亚（Bessarabia），并于1917年12月4日取得归化文件。她持有护照第264114号。
（虽然这可能只是巧合，但值得注意的是，舒纳曼出生于莱奥明斯特[Leominster]，且被认为接替了明斯特[Minster]的职务。）

When enquiries were made regarding the Shanghai Operators
Service it was found that the total sum received in fees from
the students would not be sufficient to pay the expenses
incurred in conducting the school, as there are only 12 students
paying $8 per month attending night classes. Shunaman has no
other business as far as can be ascertained, yet on May 11, 1936
his wife opened two current accounts at the National City Bank
of New York, and at the end of January 1937, deposits made by
cash totalled G$500 and C.S.$80. From this it would appear that
they have some other source of income.

Information having been received that on Christmas Eve
Shunaman invited a number of British soldiers to his school
to attend a party, arrangements were made with Capt. J.G.
Sandie, M.C. Officer-in-charge "A" Company, Loyal Regiment,
to obtain further particulars regarding the matter. So far
it has been ascertained that the soldiers met Shunaman in
a bar, and after introducing himself he gave them his card
and issued the invitation. The late passes which the soldiers
applied for to enable them to attend this party were refused,
but it is not yet known whether they did attend.

During January 1937, further enquiries were made regarding
Shunaman and from the method adopted by him in certain business
transactions it was felt that he was undoubtedly an agent of
some sort.

On Feb. 2, 1937, an official of the U.S. Consulate General
was approached and told of this suspicion, whereon he revealed
that the original enquiry was the result on a letter from
Washington D.C. in which it was stated that Shunaman was an
important member of the American Communist Party.

日期....................19

主题....................................................................................................
制作人................................................呈送人.........................

在对上海报务员服务社进行调查时发现，从学生那里收取的费用总额不足以支付办学开支，因为只有12名学生参加夜校课程，每人每月缴纳8美元。据查，舒纳曼没有其他业务，然而他的妻子于1936年5月11日在纽约国家城市银行（National City Bank of New York）开设了两个活期账户，截至1937年1月底，现金存款总计国币500元及小洋80元。由此看来，他们另有收入来源。

收到情报称，舒纳曼在圣诞前夜邀请多名英国士兵到其学校参加聚会，遂与忠义团（Loyal Regiment）A连连长、军功十字勋章获得者J.G.桑迪（J.G. Sandie）上尉作出安排，以获取有关此事的更多详情。截至目前已查明，士兵们是在一家酒吧遇见舒纳曼的，他在自我介绍后递给他们名片并发出邀请。士兵们申请延期通行证以便参加此次聚会，但被拒绝，不过目前尚不清楚他们是否最终出席。

1937年1月期间，对舒纳曼进行了进一步调查，鉴于他在某些商业交易中采取的手段，感觉他无疑是一名某种类型的代理人。

1937年2月2日，接触了美国总领事馆的一名官员并告知了这一怀疑，随后该官员透露，最初的查询源于华盛顿特区发来的一封信，信中称舒纳曼是美国共产党的重要成员。

Subject Shanghai Operators' Service and Frederic Leslie Shunsman.
Made by D.S. Jones Forwarded by J Byrne I.S.S.
The Shanghai Operators' Service, now located at No. 190
Peking Road, was formerly incorporated with the Shanghai
Nautical Academy, an institution opened up by Capt. A.C. Newton,
a master-mariner who has spent many years on the China Const
and who now, chiefly on account of his drunken habits, is
unemployed and living on charity.
Capt. Newton inaugurated the Academy named at No. 12 Rue
du Consulat in December 1935, occupying a flat on the same
floor as the Russian Mercantile Marine Association. This
marine association trains officers for the merchant service
and holds classes of instruction in wireless telegraphy.
When Newton opened up his so-called Nautical Academy, also
specialising in radio-telegraphy, in the adjoining flat the
Russians rightly or wrongly considered that he had established
himself there so that he might divert to his own establishment
the flow of pupils which would normally be expected to enter
the Russian Mercantile Marine Association.
At first a Britisher named Hulbert attended to the radio-
telegraphic side of the new venture, but there was a quarrel
between him and Newton over money matters and Hulbert cleared
out.
Shunsman appeared on the scene at about this time. He
occupied a room at the Shanghai Nautical Academy and appears
to have carried on the radio work where Hulbert left off.
The Shanghai Nautical Academy was not a success and in
April 1936 Newton shut up shop owing three months' rent to
the landlord. Shunsman moved into Room 37/38 No. 190 Peking
Road, business address of the Shanghai Operators' Service, on
August 1st. His wife interviewed the house agents and made

上海报务员服务社现位于北京路190号，原隶属于上海航海学院，该机构由A.C.牛顿船长创办。牛顿是一位资深船长，在中国沿海服役多年，目前主要因酗酒习惯而失业，靠救济生活。
牛顿船长于1935年12月在领事馆路12号创办了上述学院，占用与俄国商船协会同一楼层的一套公寓。该海事协会培训商船船员，并开设无线电报务指导课程。当牛顿在隔壁公寓开设同样专攻无线电报务的所谓航海学院时，俄国人无论对错，都认为他在那里立足是为了将原本预期会进入俄国商船协会的学生流引向自己的机构。
起初，一位名叫赫尔伯特的英国人负责这项新 ventures 的无线电报务方面工作，但他与牛顿因金钱问题发生争吵，赫尔伯特随即离开。
舒恩斯曼大约在此时出现。他在上海航海学院占据了一个房间，似乎接续了赫尔伯特留下的无线电工作。
上海航海学院经营不善，1936年4月，牛顿因拖欠房东三个月租金而关门停业。舒恩斯曼于8月1日搬入北京路190号37/38室，此处为上海报务员服务社的营业地址。他的妻子会见了房屋经纪人并做了

from the s.s. Anastasis, a small Greek owned steamer which
was broken up by the China Shipbreakers Ltd. of Shanghai about
one year ago. Its value is said to be in the neighbourhood
of $250.00 local currency. Most of the equipment at No.190

known what arrangement has been made between Newton and
Shunsman re ownership of this property.
Observation has been made at No. 190 Peking Road, but no
more than four pupils - two foreign and two Chinese - were
seen to attend the classes at one time. Shunsman conducts

Shanghai, China,

Subject: Shanghai Operators Service and Frederic
Leslie Shunaman.

Major F. W. Gerrard, C.I.E.,
Commissioner of Police,
Shanghai Municipal Council,
185 Foochow Road,
Shanghai, China.

Sir: Confidential

I have the honor to state that an American citizen
named Frederic Leslie Shunaman, who stated that he has
been residing at Shanghai since December 6, 1935, has
filed at this Consulate General an application for the
registration of the Shanghai Operators Service, Rooms
37-38, 190 Peking Road, Shanghai. He stated further
that his firm is a school which teaches radio telegraphy
and the servicing of all sending and receiving radio
equipment, and that the school, which has been in opera-
tion since April, 1936, has at present seven pupils.
Mr. Shunaman was born in the United States of a naturalized
father and was married on January 27, 1932, to Miss Yetta
Cabin, who was born in Russia, and who is also residing at
Shanghai.

The Consulate General would greatly appreciate receiving
a report on Mr. Shunaman, especially one containing informa-
tion regarding his radio equipment and the type of persons
with whom he and his wife associate.
